author: CC
prose: A process that strips CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID outlives the tester's run in that run's mount namespace and keeps the swap mounted. Measured 2026-11-18 on akienasus: inside a sealed `bin/cairn test --exec`, a `setsid` child carrying the run's id was gone 4 s after the run returned (kill_what_it_started, bf3c16162827, collects by environment), while an `env -u CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID setsid` child outlived the sandbox, still in the run's mount namespace (mnt 4026532367, ~/.cairn dev 40 against the live 2050), holding the swap mounted until it was ended by hand (n=1). The tester's bwrap passes neither --die-with-parent nor --unshare-pid, so the sandbox does not end its children. No standing spawn site strips the id today. One possible shape for whoever picks it up: the tester's stop also collects processes by mount namespace, not only by environment.
